body:
The order in which each lampOS builder takes its tasks. Kept by the first builder (the one with lamp-4ace); only it edits this body. Decided by the owner and the first builder on 2026-10-14 (`fifth-P3`), replacing the list in `lampOS/docs/work-split.md`, which keeps the rules, the loops, "What the lamp showed" and the history of finished tasks.

**A builder's next task:** the first issue in its own list below that is open and not `status:taken`. Claim it as `lampOS/docs/joining.md` says ("Tasks as GitHub issues"): add `status:taken`, comment `taken by <name> · session <id> · <lamp or none>`, then read the comments again and release it if the first "taken" comment is not yours. Questions and answers are comments on the task's issue. A proposal is a new issue labelled `proposal` and `builder:<name>`; the first builder answers it in a comment, and no answer means not allowed. A finished task is handed back as one pull request from `<name>/<task>` into `lamp-voice`, not a draft, with its ARM64 run green (joining.md, "One pull request per task", `fifth-P6`, decided 18:33); the first builder merges it after its minute on lamp-4ace, and the merge closes the issue.

Owner's order of 2026-10-14, 14:00: parts that stand on their own first, the harder ones later. And at 17:22: "reimagine the entire experience. make lamp the most fun creature to interact with": the design is `lampOS/docs/creature.md`; its pieces (#710-#714) come first. Stopping and interruption are tested by the first builder in the evenings.

## Every component of the brain first (the owner, 2026-10-15 about 07:00)

"in the mvp, did you build ALL the components of the brain? and now have builders perfect/optimize each of those components?" Not yet. These parts of `lampOS/docs/brain-build.md` are missing, or only watching, on lamp-4ace, and each now has a builder. When every row works with the others, each builder owns a set of components to perfect.

| Component (brain-build step) | On lamp-4ace | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Policy deciding when the lamp speaks first (8) | Watches only; decides nothing | **#752 (second)**: progress news through Jev, acting; then hello |
| Who is talking to the lamp: both microphones and the face (7) | The two microphones are never used together | **#753 (fourth)**, after #749 |
| A second voice when Gemini is down (11) | Says it cannot hear just now | **#754 (third)**: proposal first |
| The privacy switch (9) | Read by nothing | **#755 (third)** |
| Questions around a task: a yes in two breaths (6) | Lost about 3 in 5 | **#736 (first, while the second is on #752)**: fix on lamp-4ace 07:00, being played |
| A second agent engine: Codex and the others (8) | Claude Code only | **#733 (fourth)**, after #753 |
| What the owner teaches and corrects (8) | Covered in part: "remember …" is kept and told to every session. The Policy does not use it | With #752's follow-up (second) |
| The body at power-up, giving way to a hand (12, safety) | Started by hand | **#702, #703 (fifth)** |
| Recognising who is there, memory for each person (4) | Not built | After the rows above (fifth: the eyes) |
| Setup, network, reset, operator pages (12) | Not built; setup waits on the owner's choice | #699 (third) for the operator's side; setup stays out until the owner decides |

## The V2 MVP first: wide, then deep (the owner, 2026-10-15 00:37)

"prioritize the tasks for builders with ruthless priority. so we have an end to end experience on lamp first. then we'll optimize each component and edge cases later … wide first. deep later … have all the pieces in place make sure the whole works. then after that, have builders optimize each component."

So until every piece below is on lamp-4ace and works with the others, a builder works only on its MVP tasks. Everything else waits under "After the MVP", even if already taken: pause it, push what you have, and say so on its issue.

**Never idle, until V2 is done** (the owner, 2026-10-15 about 06:48: "not just finishing the mvp, but keep building until v2 is done!"). If every MVP task in your list is waiting (on a lamp, a person, the owner's key or a review), take your next task under "After the MVP" and keep going. Say on the waiting issue what it waits on. When an MVP task becomes possible again, it comes first.

| What a person gets | State on lamp-4ace (2026-10-15 00:40) | Missing piece, and whose |
|---|---|---|
| Talk to it naturally: turns, interruptions, noise | On and working | — |
| It looks alive: body, light, the eye, breathing, sleep at night | On. It fell asleep at 01:45 as designed, then a false name hearing woke it 2 s later. The eye has not yet been seen working with a person | **#749 (fourth)**; the eye: first builder with a person today |
| It sees you: turns to your face, hello when you arrive, turns to a call, "what do you see?" | Turning to a face and to a call: on. **The hello was only recording, and in 680 sessions it was never once due**; it is switched to speaking today. Sight was built and kept off by the character line; it is switched on today | first builder: both switched on at the next voice restart and tried with a person this morning |
| It does things: light, volume | On | — |
| Reminders and timers by voice | **On since 04:39** (#747 merged): "set a timer for one minute" → "One minute, starting now." … "Your timer is done."; reminders set, listed, cancelled and said when due | third: a reminder "in two minutes" comes up to a minute early (follow-up on #747) |
| It remembers you, across days | **On since 02:47** (#743 merged): "what did we talk about yesterday?" answered from last night | — |
| It works for you: hands tasks to Claude Code and tells you the result | **Works end to end**: the played day at 01:25 handed a poem to Claude Code and told the result unasked 39 s later | **#736 (second)**: a yes in two breaths still lost; #740's first try failed its minute (it ended the voice whenever news was told) |
| You can touch it: button, base strip, head pads | Button on; touch merged 01:17, off until tuned with a hand | **#711 (third), first builder at the lamp today** |
| It starts by itself after power, and every part comes back | Every part enabled at boot (the eyes since 01:32) except the body, started by hand until #703; the body's wake from fold shown; a power cut not tried | **#702, then #701 (fifth)** |
| It is safe: gives way to a hand, never hurts itself | Not built | **#703 (fifth)** |
| It gets new software by itself | **Works** (#741 merged): at 03:48 lamp-4ace updated itself to build 188 from a signed test channel, every part well. Publishing waits on the owner's signing key | **#737 (second)**: the `publish:` job; the owner: the key |

How a lamp is set up (phone, desktop) is not decided by the owner and is not in the MVP yet.

The first builder plays the whole lamp end to end every evening (a person's day: arrive, talk, ask, hand over work, get news, a reminder, touch, leave, night) and files each fault as an issue to a builder with room.

### second
1. #752 — 48. The Policy decides when the lamp speaks first: progress news (part 3 of #732, with its voice side), then hello
2. #737 — 45. Updates: the `publish:` job, ready for the owner's key

#736 (the two-breath yes) is with the first builder for now; #740 stays open for your notes. Later: #723 (the early end), #694 (the bare name; #750 not installed)

### first (the first builder's own, while a builder is away)
1. #736 — 44. The yes in two breaths: the model is told why a call was not done (`d128c458a`, on lamp-4ace 07:00), five two-breath runs next
2. #712 — 34. The eye (waits for a person at the lamp)
3. Lamp minutes for every pull request, the evening's whole-lamp play, the review page

### third
1. Follow-up to #747: a time from now ("in two minutes") goes to `set_timer`, not a rounded `set_reminder` (MVP)
2. #711 — 33. Touch: #728 merged 01:17 (its minute without `--touch` passed). Turned on with a person at the lamp today: thresholds, E4/E8, then on by default (MVP)
3. #755 — 51. The microphone privacy switch (small)
4. #754 — 50. A second voice when Gemini is down: a proposal comment first

After the MVP: #699 — 8. A shared log, settings, and reports from the parts that give none

Done: #695 — 6 (on lamp-4ace since 16:53) · #696 — 11 (on `lamp-voice`; off on lamp-4ace until the voice uses it)

### fourth
1. #749 — 47. A sleeping lamp wakes on its name only when a person's voice is heard with it (MVP: last night a false name hearing woke it 2 s after it fell asleep)
2. #753 — 49. Who is talking to the lamp: both microphones and the face, as one signal on the bus
3. #733 — 41. Codex and the others: the person names who gets the work (moved from the second)

After the MVP: #739 (the timed tests; paused at 06:50 after seven loaded runs). Next, the faults the first builder's end-to-end runs find.

Done: #698 — 29 (pull request #743, merged 02:51; on lamp-4ace since 02:47) · #697 — 28 (on lamp-4ace since 2026-10-14 16:54) · #713 — 35 (pull request #727, merged 23:01) · #707 — 30 (pull request #721, merged; on lamp-4ace since 20:21) · #700 — 17 (pull request #722, merged)

### fifth
1. #702 — 23. Waking up after the power comes back: now the whole lamp, every part, from power (MVP)
2. #701 — 27. The keeper (MVP)
3. #703 — 24. Giving way to a hand, and not hurting itself (MVP)

After the MVP: #720 (seeing someone speak; pause it), #704 (weighing and measuring the lamp)

Done: #715 — 37 (pull request #724, merged 01:00; on lamp-4ace with `--look-at-name on` since 00:57) · #710 — 32 (pull request #718, merged; on lamp-4ace since 18:41) · #719 — 38 (pull request #726, merged 23:00; its body on lamp-4ace)

comments.body: First builder, 2026-10-14 17:38, to every builder: the ARM64 run's failure in `crates/controls/tests/program.rs` (`sigterm_finishes_recording_and_releases_the_actual_serve_owner`, `No such file or directory`) was the workflow's, not your code: the Debian 12 container lacked `/bin/kill` (procps). Fixed on `lamp-voice` (`.github/workflows/lampos-arm64.yml`); rebase onto it and the run should pass. Do not change that test for it.

First builder, 2026-10-14 18:23, to every builder: the second ARM64 failure, `crates/surround/tests/selection.rs` (`interrupted_collection_leaves_only_unaccepted_files_and_retry_removes_them`), was the workflow again: the Debian container ran the tests as root, and root ignores the read-only folder the test relies on. Fixed on `lamp-voice` (`91a0fdb3a`): the job now runs on GitHub's Ubuntu 22.04 ARM machine as an ordinary user (glibc 2.35, so its binaries run on the lamps' Debian 12). Rebase onto it; do not change that test. If a run still fails on something that passes on your Mac, say it on your task's issue and I look at the workflow first.

First builder, 19:36, to every builder: the ARM64 run is green on `lamp-voice` for the first time (run 38559471390, `21c24fc0a`: Ubuntu 22.04 on ARM64, as an ordinary user, whole workspace built and tested one test at a time). What had kept it red was the workflow (no `procps`; tests run as root) and one Records open that only fails when not root (`O_NOATIME`, mended in `21c24fc0a`). Since `652a196e1` `cargo clippy -p lamp-body --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passes on Linux. Rebase your task branches on `origin/lamp-voice`; a pull request is ready when its own run is green (joining.md, "One pull request per task"). On a Mac, run `lamp-body` and `lamp-voice` tests with `-- --test-threads=1`: some of their tests fail in parallel there.
